necessary_context.content: E:R^d×Lambda→R and L_lambda:R^d→R. Eq.(2) selects the infimum of E over inner global minimizers. Under uniqueness, Eq.(7) reduces to f(lambda)=E(w_lambda,lambda), where w_lambda=argmin_u L_lambda(u).
necessary_context.name: Bilevel objectives

necessary_context.content: For positive integer T, w_{0,lambda}=Phi_0(lambda), w_{t,lambda}=Phi_t(w_{t-1,lambda},lambda), t=1,...,T. Phi_0:R^m→R^d and Phi_t:R^d×R^m→R^d are smooth. The approximate objective is f_T(lambda)=E(w_{T,lambda},lambda).
necessary_context.name: Finite dynamics

necessary_context.content: Task-specific parameters are stacked in w; lambda is shared. Eqs.(3),(4) sum training and validation losses over tasks. Algorithm 1 receives an episode batch B and returns the gradient sum over B, without normalization.
necessary_context.name: Task separation and batch

necessary_context.content: Theorem 3.1 uses (i)–(iv). Theorem 3.2 additionally requires (v) a Lipschitz constant for E in w uniform in lambda and (vi) uniform convergence of the inner iterates over Lambda.
necessary_context.name: Uniformity assumptions
